roles.name: AI / Machine Learning Engineer
roles.oneLiner: Builds systems that learn from data and deploy AI/ML models to production at scale.
roles.quickPitch: An ML Engineer builds systems that learn from data and make predictions or decisions — like fraud detection, recommendation engines ("customers also bought…"), or chatbots. They take models from experiments and turn them into reliable software running in production.
dayToDay: Collect and prepare data for training models.
Train, test and improve machine learning / deep learning models.
Deploy models into apps and APIs so real users can use them.
Monitor model accuracy over time and retrain when performance drops.
Increasingly: build applications on top of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT, Claude, Llama.

keyTerms.definition: Software that learns patterns from data instead of being hand-coded with rules.
The "trained brain" produced by learning from data.
Training = teaching the model; inference = using it to make a prediction.
Supervised learns from labelled examples; unsupervised finds patterns in unlabelled data.
ML using layered networks loosely inspired by the brain; powers image, speech and language AI.
Large Language Model — AI trained on huge text data to understand and generate language.
AI for text/language / AI for images and video.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation — giving an LLM access to company documents so it answers using them.
DevOps practices applied to ML: deploying, versioning and monitoring models.
Further training an existing model on specific data to specialise it.

roles.toolsSummary: Python; PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn; Hugging Face; LangChain/LlamaIndex; MLflow, Kubeflow; Docker, Kubernetes; AWS SageMaker, Azure ML, Google Vertex AI; vector databases (Pinecone, FAISS); SQL.

crossQuestions.q: What's the difference between an ML Engineer and a Data Scientist?
crossQuestions.a: A Data Scientist mainly analyses data and builds models to find insights; an ML Engineer focuses on building and deploying those models into production software at scale. There's overlap, and we position your profile based on which side your experience leans.

crossQuestions.q: Is GenAI/LLM experience important now?
crossQuestions.a: Yes, many current AI job descriptions mention LLMs, RAG or GenAI. If you've built anything with them, we'll highlight it prominently.

crossQuestions.q: I only have academic projects.
crossQuestions.a: That's common for entry-level candidates. Strong GitHub projects with clear results, plus a cloud ML certification, help close the gap.

crossQuestions.q: Do you know MLOps?
crossQuestions.a: It's the practice of reliably deploying, versioning and monitoring ML models — basically DevOps for machine learning, with tools like MLflow, Kubeflow and SageMaker.

quiz.q: What is the key difference between a Data Scientist and an ML Engineer?
options: Data Scientists build and maintain hardware servers; ML Engineers write web pages.
Data Scientists focus on analyzing data and finding insights; ML Engineers focus on building and deploying models into scalable production software.
ML Engineers only work with spreadsheets, while Data Scientists only program in C++.
There is no difference; they are identical job titles with identical day-to-day tasks.
quiz.explanation: Data Scientists uncover insights and develop initial models, whereas ML Engineers take those models and engineer robust, production-ready software systems around them.

quiz.q: What does RAG stand for in modern AI application development?
options: Random Automated Generation
Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Recursive Algorithm Gradients
Real-time Analytical Graphing
quiz.explanation: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds an LLM by pulling relevant knowledge/documents from a vector database before generating an answer.

quiz.q: What is MLOps?
options: A brand of machine learning computer processors.
DevOps practices applied to machine learning: automating deployment, monitoring, and versioning of ML models.
A legal compliance document required for training neural networks in California.
An open-source spreadsheet used for manual data labeling.
quiz.explanation: MLOps applies continuous integration, deployment, and monitoring practices to ML models in production (e.g. using tools like MLflow, Kubeflow, SageMaker).

Ruby on Rails

quiz.explanation: PyTorch (along with TensorFlow) is the standard deep learning framework in research and modern AI production.

Promise them a $200k salary if they take one 10-minute online tutorial.

roles.name: Data Scientist
roles.oneLiner: Uses data, statistics and machine learning to answer business questions and predict outcomes.
roles.quickPitch: A Data Scientist uses data, statistics and programming to answer business questions and predict outcomes — for example, which customers might cancel, or how much stock to order. They turn raw data into insights and recommendations.
dayToDay: Gather and clean data from databases and files.
Explore data to find trends and patterns (EDA).
Build statistical and machine learning models to predict outcomes.
Run experiments such as A/B tests.
Present findings through dashboards and presentations to business teams.

keyTerms.definition: Exploratory Data Analysis — first look at data to understand it.

Predicting a number (price) / predicting a category (yes/no, spam/not spam).
Comparing two versions to see which performs better.
Statistical way to check if a result is real or chance.
Creating useful input variables for a model.
When a model memorises training data and fails on new data.
Charts and dashboards that explain data.
Data too large for normal tools; handled with Spark, Hadoop.
Builds the pipelines that move and store data; Data Scientists use that data.

crossQuestions.q: Data Analyst vs Data Scientist?
crossQuestions.a: Analysts focus on reporting and explaining what happened (SQL, Excel, dashboards). Scientists go further, predicting what will happen using statistics and ML. Many candidates target both titles, and we can market you for both if your skills fit.

crossQuestions.q: Do I need a Master's?
crossQuestions.a: It's common but not mandatory; strong projects, SQL/Python skills and relevant experience can compensate.

crossQuestions.q: Which is more important, Python or SQL?
crossQuestions.a: Both. SQL appears in almost every data job description; Python is standard for analysis and modelling.

crossQuestions.q: Do I need experience with Big Data tools like Spark or Hadoop for entry/mid roles?
crossQuestions.a: For entry to mid-level roles, strong Python (Pandas/NumPy/scikit-learn) and advanced SQL are the core essentials; distributed big data tools like Spark or Databricks are usually valued bonuses or required for senior roles. We position your resume highlighting data analysis and measurable modeling impact.

options: When a computer case is too small for the graphics card.
When a model memorizes training data so closely that it performs poorly on new, unseen data.
When a dataset has too many duplicate rows deleted.
When an algorithm finishes training in less than 5 minutes.
quiz.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise and specific details of the training set instead of generalized underlying patterns.

options: Photoshop and Canva
Python and SQL
AutoCAD and SolidWorks
Ruby and Swift

quiz.q: What is an A/B test?

A controlled experiment comparing two versions (A and B) to determine which produces better performance or user engagement.
An automated unit test checking code indentation.
A grading scale for data warehouse cleanliness.

roles.name: Data Engineer
roles.oneLiner: Designs, builds, and maintains the data pipelines and infrastructure that deliver clean, reliable data for analytics and AI.
roles.quickPitch: A Data Engineer builds the digital plumbing of a company — extracting data from databases, apps, and logs, cleaning it, and loading it into data warehouses like Snowflake or BigQuery. They ensure data scientists and business analysts have fresh, accurate, and reliable data ready to use.
dayToDay: Design, build, and maintain scalable ETL/ELT pipelines using tools like Apache Spark, Airflow, and dbt.
Ingest data from diverse sources (APIs, transactional SQL databases, event streams like Kafka) into central data lakes or warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks).
Optimize query performance, data partitioning, indexing, and storage costs across cloud platforms.
Implement automated data quality checks, schema evolution tests, and monitoring alerts for pipeline failures.
Collaborate with Data Scientists, Software Developers, and BI Analysts to provide production-ready tables and feature stores.

keyTerms.definition: Extract, Transform, Load (or Extract, Load, Transform) — the process of copying data from sources, reshaping it, and loading it into an analytical warehouse.
An automated series of steps that moves data from where it's created to where it can be analyzed.
A centralized database optimized for fast business reporting and analytics (e.g., Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift).
A vast storage repository that holds raw, unstructured or semi-structured data in its native format until needed (e.g., AWS S3, Azure Data Lake).
Batch processes data in scheduled chunks (e.g., nightly); streaming processes each record instantly in real-time as it occurs (e.g., Kafka).
A fast, distributed engine for processing massive datasets across clusters of computers.
A workflow scheduler that manages when each data task runs, handles retries, and enforces task dependencies.
A tool that lets data teams transform raw warehouse data using simple SQL select statements and automated testing.
The architectural blueprint organizing warehouse tables into facts (numbers) and dimensions (context like dates, customers).
Tracking the origin and journey of data, and validating that rows are accurate, complete, and not duplicated.

crossQuestions.q: What is the difference between a Data Engineer, a Data Scientist, and a Data Analyst?
crossQuestions.a: A Data Engineer builds and maintains the pipelines and databases that deliver clean data; a Data Analyst examines that data to answer business questions; and a Data Scientist builds machine learning models to predict future trends. We position your profile clearly around your pipeline building and infrastructure strengths.

crossQuestions.q: Is Big Data (Spark, Kafka) required for every Data Engineer role, or is SQL/dbt enough?
crossQuestions.a: Many modern companies focus heavily on the Modern Data Stack (SQL + dbt + Snowflake/BigQuery) for business analytics; massive scale tech or streaming companies require Spark and Kafka. We highlight whichever stack you excel in to match the right job postings.

crossQuestions.q: Should I learn AWS, Azure, or GCP for Data Engineering?
crossQuestions.a: AWS and Azure have the highest overall job volume, while GCP is prominent in startup and analytics-heavy environments. Mastering one primary cloud data stack (e.g. AWS S3 + Glue + Redshift, or Azure Data Factory + Synapse/Databricks) is what recruiters look for, and skills transfer easily.

crossQuestions.q: How do I make my resume stand out without 5+ years of experience?
crossQuestions.a: Recruiters love measurable efficiency and scale: highlight the volume of data processed (e.g. 'processed 5M daily events'), cost savings on cloud warehouse compute, pipeline execution speedups (e.g. 'reduced ETL runtime from 4 hours to 45 minutes'), and include a public GitHub repo with an automated Airflow + dbt pipeline.

To configure local office Wi-Fi routers and printers.
quiz.explanation: ETL/ELT pipelines extract raw data from disparate operational systems, reshape/clean it, and load it into an analytical data warehouse for reporting and machine learning.

options: Apache Airflow
Figma
AutoCAD
Wireshark

quiz.q: What is the difference between a Data Warehouse and a Data Lake?
options: A Data Warehouse is only stored on USB flash drives; a Data Lake is an on-premises physical pond.
A Data Warehouse stores structured, schema-on-write data optimized for fast SQL queries; a Data Lake stores vast amounts of raw data in various formats (structured, semi-structured, unstructured).
A Data Warehouse is only used by human resources; a Data Lake is only used by civil engineers.
There is no difference; the terms are 100% interchangeable in enterprise architecture.
quiz.explanation: Data warehouses (like Snowflake or BigQuery) enforce schemas for fast analytical SQL, whereas data lakes (like AWS S3) store raw files in native formats (Parquet, JSON, CSV) prior to transformation.

quiz.q: What role does dbt (data build tool) play in modern data engineering?
options: It replaces Python entirely for machine learning inference.
It allows data teams to write modular SQL transformation logic directly inside the data warehouse, complete with version control and automated data tests.
It is an optical character recognition tool for scanning paper documents.
It is a network firewall used to block DDoS attacks.
quiz.explanation: dbt enables the 'T' in ELT by allowing engineers and analytics engineers to transform raw warehouse data using modular SQL SELECT queries, documentation, and automated assertions.

quiz.q: What is Apache Spark primarily used for in Big Data engineering?
options: Fast, distributed in-memory data processing across large clusters of machines for massive datasets.
Editing vector graphics and company logos.
Measuring electrical voltage in utility power grids.
Sending bulk email marketing newsletters.
quiz.explanation: Apache Spark is a distributed computing engine that processes huge volumes of data in parallel memory across clusters, dramatically outperforming traditional MapReduce.
